Center]] |champion = [[Bahamas Championship|Baha Mar Hoops]] champions |tourney = |tourney_result = }} {{2021–22 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2021–22 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Louisville]] during the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games on Denny Crum Court at the [[KFC Yum! Center]] in [[Downtown Louisville|downtown Louisville, Kentucky]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. They were led by interim head coach [[Mike Pegues]]. The Cardinals finished the season 13–19 overall and 6–14 in [[2021–22 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for eleventh place. As the eleventh seed in the [[2022 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]], they defeated fourteenth seed [[2021–22 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] in the First Round before losing to sixth seed [[2021–22 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] in the Second Round. Head coach [[Chris Mack (basketball)|Chris Mack]] was fired on January 26, 2022, after starting the season 11–9.{{Cite web |last=Lyons |first=Dan |title=Louisville Basketball Makes Official Decision on Coach Chris Mack |url=https://www.si.com/college/2022/01/26/chris-mack-fired-louisville-basketball-official |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}} Associate coach Mike Pegues was named the interim coach for the remainder of the season.{{Cite web |date=2022-01-26 |title=Mack out at Louisville: 'You've gotta win games' |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33153259/chris-mack-acknowledges-louisville-cardinals-men-basketball-coach |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} On March 16, the school named former Louisville player [[Kenny Payne]] the team's new head coach.{{Cite web |title=Louisville hires Kenny Payne: Cardinals set to introduce ex-player, former Kentucky assistant as new coach |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/louisville-hires-kenny-payne-cardinals-set-to-introduce-ex-player-former-kentucky-assistant-as-new-coach/ |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} ==Previous season== In a [[2020-21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|season]] limited due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], the [[2020-21 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Cardinals]] finished the season 13–7, 8–5 to finish in seventh place in [[2020–21 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]]. They lost to [[2020–21 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the second round of the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. They were listed as an alternate team for the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]should a team be unable to participate due to COVID-19 issues.{{cite web|url=https://gocards.com/news/2021/3/15/louisville-is-first-alternate-for-ncaa-mens-basketball-tournament.aspx|title=Louisville is First Alternate for NCAA men's basketball tournament}} The team declined an invitation to the [[2021 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] prior to the NCAA Tournament field being announced.{{cite web|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/ncaabk/ncaa-tournament-snubs-louisville-duke-among-teams-to-turn-down-nit/ar-BB1eAa0F|title=NCAA tournament snubs Louisville, Duke among teams to turn down NIT|publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]]}}{{Cite web|last=Russell|first=Shannon|title=Louisville basketball denied bid into 2021 NCAA Tournament, won't accept NIT invite|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2021/03/14/ncaa-tournament-2021-louisville-basketball-opponent-bracket/4624932001/|access-date=2021-09-16|website=The Courier-Journal|language=en-US}} When all teams were able to participate in the opening rounds of the NCAA tournament, the Cardinals season ended.{{Cite web|last=Conway|first=Tyler|title=All 68 2021 NCAA Tournament Teams Cleared to Play After COVID-19 Testing|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2936685-all-68-2021-ncaa-tournament-teams-cleared-to-play-after-covid-19-testing|access-date=2021-09-16|website=Bleacher Report|language=en}} ==Offseason== ===Suspension of Chris Mack=== On August 27, 2021, the school announced that head coach Chris Mack would be suspended for the first six games of the season due to his part in an attempt by former assistant [[Dino Gaudio]] to blackmail Mack.{{Cite web|last=Forde|first=Pat|title=Mack Feels Wrath of Ongoing Louisville Scandal Fallout|url=https://www.si.com/college/2021/08/27/chris-mack-suspended-louisville-dino-gaudio|access-date=2021-09-16|website=Sports Illustrated|language=en-us}} Gaudio, who was a longtime assistant to Mack and whom Mack had let go following the completion of the 2020–21 season, had attempted to blackmail Mack with allegations of relatively minor misconduct by Mack and the team in violation of NCAA rules. The school said that Mack was being suspended for failing to follow university guidelines regarding the matter.{{Cite web|date=2021-08-27|title=Louisville suspends Mack six games without pay|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32096612/louisville-cardinals-suspend-men-basketball-coach-chris-mack-six-games-role-extortion-case|access-date=2021-09-16|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} Gaudio pled guilty to extortion for his actions in the matter.{{Cite web|title=Louisville suspends coach Chris Mack for first six games of upcoming season for breaking school rules|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/louisville-suspends-coach-chris-mack-for-first-six-games-of-upcoming-season-for-breaking-school-rules/|access-date=2021-09-16|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}} ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" style="text-align:center;" |+ style="{{CollegePrimaryStyle|Louisville Cardinals|color=white|border=no}}" | Departures |- align=center {{CollegeSecondaryHeader|team=Louisville Cardinals| Name| Number| Pos.| Height| Weight| Year| Hometown|class8=unsortable| Reason for departure}} |- | [[Carlik Jones]] || 1 || G || 6'1" || 185 || GS Senior || [[Cincinnati|Cincinnati, OH]] || Graduated/undrafted in [[2021 NBA draft]] |- | Hogan Orbaugh || 3 || C || 6'8" || 235 || Sophomore || [[Zionsville, Indiana|Zionsville, IN]] || Walk-on;
